// Leak (c): LAUNDER A FOREIGN RESPONSE THROUGH NewReplay.
//
// Replay is the one channel every class reads, because a replay carries no payload and is
// therefore a control. Laundering takes a response that DID carry a payload, wipes the stamps and
// the wire record, and hands it to NewReplay, which then shares it with everybody.
//
// NewReplay itself is exported and always will be: the runner has to build controls. What kills
// this is the first line, not the last. To launder a FOREIGN response you must first hold one,
// and the only accessor that ever handed one over was p.Obs(as ClassID). A reviewer showed that
// p.Obs(p.Owner()) returned a foreign response with a nil error, because Owner() and Obs read the
// same authoritative vault entry, so they always agreed. There is now no accessor that takes an
// owner at all: a class is handed triage.OwnedResponses, which is already only its own.
package leakfixture

import "ars0n-framework-v2-server/utils/triage"

func leakLaunder(foreign triage.Perturbed) (triage.Replay, error) {
	obs, err := foreign.Obs(foreign.Owner())
	if err != nil {
		return triage.Replay{}, err
	}
	obs.Kind = triage.ObsBaseline
	obs.Class = triage.ClassNone
	obs.ProbeOrdinal = 0
	obs.Payload = triage.PayloadWire{}
	obs.Marker = ""
	obs.MarkerPos = ""
	return triage.NewReplay(obs)
}
